title: Data-sovereignty guardrail: retention engine, telemetry, and evacuation gating for VPC/private
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a composable data-sovereignty guardrail that enforces tenant-level retention windows and residency affinity for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments, surfaces verifiable evidence to customers and auditors, and prevents automatic region evacuation/failover for customers with strict jurisdiction constraints unless explicit playbook approvals occur. This ticket covers the policy engine, control-plane flags, evidence pipeline, and the failover gating flow (operator/UI + automation).
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine implements per-tenant residency_affinity and retention_window settings configurable via Console API
Control plane exposes immutable residency_assertion artifacts (signed manifest) that can be downloaded for audits
Automatic region failover respects residency_affinity: tenants marked 'region-locked' are not involuntarily evacuated without an approved evacuation ticket and audit trail
Retention enforcement runs on object-store lifecycle hooks and produces retention reports daily to an S3-compatible bucket that is region-bound
Console shows per-tenant residency dashboard: current region, retention window, last evidence snapshot, and evacuation block status
End-to-end e2e test covering policy change, attempted cross-region failover, blocked flow and audit evidence generation

decisions: Use tenant-scoped signed residency manifests (KMS-backed) instead of global proof artifacts to reduce blast radius and simplify key rotation

Evacuation gating will be implemented as a three-step flow: automated detect -> operator review (Console UI) -> explicit 'evacuate-override' signed by two approvers; default behaviour will be to block for 'region-locked' tenants
Retention enforcement will use a hybrid approach: object-store lifecycle policies where possible + server-side periodic scrubbing job for legacy/third-party stores
Policy evaluation will be cached in-memory per control-plane instance with a TTL and consistent hashing for low-latency checks during routing/failover decisions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Forced failover may be needed during catastrophic outages -> Mitigation: provide an explicit emergency override path with required approver audit + an automated rollback playbook
Risk: Evidence tampering or accidental disclosure -> Mitigation: sign manifests with tenant KMS and write immutable copies to an append-only audit store with WORM-like retention
Risk: Performance impact on routing layer -> Mitigation: optimize policy lookups with local cache and precompute affinity decisions during request admission
open_questions: Should we allow per-model residency exceptions (e.g., embeddings processed in another region) or limit exception surface to whole-tenant only?
Operationally, who can approve emergency evacuation overrides for enterprise tenants? (proposal: two approvers from SRE and security)
Do we expose a machine-readable signed residency assertion API for customers to pull periodically or only a downloadable artifact?
